correctness.rationale: Reconstructed original Akima rule with g_i=|d_{i+1}-d_i| and local derivative a_i=(g_i d_{i-1}+g_{i-2} d_i)/(g_i+g_{i-2}) except zero-weight midpoint fallback. Only critical knots g_{i-2}=g_i=0 and d_{i-1}!=d_i permit nonunique limits; elsewhere slopes converge uniquely. At finitely many critical knots the ratio constraints involve pairs of zero gap indices (i-2,i), whose graph is a disjoint union of finite paths, so arbitrary endpoint/interior ratios can be achieved simultaneously by recursively chosen positive gaps vanishing at suitable rates. Integrate perturbed secants to data, then Hermite interpolation maps independent critical slopes to nonoverlapping two-cell basis bumps psi_i. Each bump has sharp sup 4/27 and TV 16/27, and critical indices differ by at least two; hence exact independent product box, sup diameter (4/27) max|Delta_i|, TV diameter (16/27) sum|Delta_i|, and iff continuity criterion in C1_loc. Independently verified two neighboring critical ratio choices t=1/3,u=2/5 and exact 4/27,16/27 Hermite constants; infinite simultaneous statement rests on the acyclic gap-graph construction.

value.rationale: This is a natural numerical-analysis stability/continuity classification of the canonical Akima interpolant at all finite collections of degenerate slope weights. The path-graph compatibility lemma turns potentially coupled neighboring weight ratios into independently selectable critical derivatives. The sharp simultaneous sup/TV diameters quantify method sensitivity beyond the known one-corner anecdote; this is a meaningful finite-dimensional structural result relevant to shape interpolation.
